real_conflicts: The proposal to increase the font weight and size of the artist name 'ELARA VANCE' (from the completeness verdict) risks creating a typographic clash. The current design relies on a delicate balance between the heavy, solid Serif title and the ethereal, widely-spaced artist name. Making the artist name 'bold' would destroy the 'whisper' aesthetic and introduce a heavy sans-serif weight that conflicts with the 'fragile' theme of the exhibition.

The proposal to brighten the 'OPEN DAILY' text (from the simplicity verdict) to high contrast contradicts the atmospheric 'dark mode' palette. While legibility is important, forcing the footer text to match the brightness of the main title disrupts the visual hierarchy and the immersive, low-light environment established by the background.
accepted: The proposal to replace the stark white 'Reserve Tickets' button with a 'ghost' style button (transparent background, thin border) is fully accepted. This aligns the functional element with the artistic language of the page, removing the visual 'shout' that breaks the immersive experience.
The proposal to introduce a subtle atmospheric gradient behind the artwork is accepted, provided it remains subtle enough to not overpower the geometric line work.
concession: I concede that the current opacity of the artist name is too low for immediate identification. However, I refuse to solve this by adding weight (boldness). Instead, I concede to increasing the *opacity* and *tracking* (letter-spacing) to make it more visible while maintaining its delicate, spectral character.
compromise: We will unify the visual language by replacing the white button with a transparent, yellow-bordered 'ghost' button. Simultaneously, we will fix the legibility of the artist name by increasing its opacity to 90% and slightly increasing the letter-spacing, rather than changing the font weight. This ensures the name is readable without introducing a heavy typographic style that clashes with the title.
nonnegotiable: The 'Reserve Tickets' button must not use a solid white background. It must be transparent or textured to maintain the atmospheric integrity of the dark palette.
